agentCan: Fill the dashboard creation form and register redirect URIs (given a logged-in session)
Implement the full Authorization Code / PKCE flow and token refresh in your codebase
Probe which endpoints respond for dev-mode apps and report gaps

approval.cost: Free to apply; your dev account needs Spotify Premium for development mode to function
approval.trigger: Quota Extension Request, required to go beyond 5 allowlisted users. Since May 15, 2025 Spotify only accepts applications from organizations (not individuals): established legal entity, active launched service, 250k+ MAU, availability in key markets, commercial viability.
approval.wait: Up to 6 weeks (stated); processing times explicitly not guaranteed

blockers.detail: Development mode caps you at 5 manually allowlisted users. Extended Quota Mode (unlimited users) has required since May 2025 an established organization with at least 250,000 monthly active users. For a new agent builder this is a catch-22, not a waiting period.
blockers.howToClear: There is no documented exception path. Design for a 5-tester pilot, or pick a different provider until you qualify. Do not promise users a Spotify connection you cannot graduate.
blockers.title: The 5-user / 250k-MAU wall

blockers.detail: The app owner's account must hold Spotify Premium for a development-mode app to function at all.
blockers.howToClear: Budget the subscription before you start; it is a stated requirement, not a recommendation.
blockers.title: Premium required to develop

blockers.detail: In extended quota mode, your scopes are frozen to what the review approved; new scopes need a separate extension request.
blockers.howToClear: Design your full scope list conservatively but completely before requesting extension.
blockers.title: Scopes lock at review time

sources.label: Quota modes (5 users, allowlist, Premium, org-only extensions, 250k MAU, 6 weeks)

flavor.recommended: Standard dashboard app, Authorization Code flow (PKCE if the token exchange runs client-side)
flavor.why: There are no editions of a Spotify app; the only thing that varies is quota mode. Register one app, pick scopes per authorization request, and plan to operate in Development Mode.

humanMust: Own the Spotify account and hold Premium on it
Accept the Developer Terms of Service + Design Guidelines
Retrieve and safeguard the client secret
Supply each tester's Spotify email for the allowlist
Submit the quota-extension request (org-only) and respond to review feedback by email
name: Spotify
nuances: Quota (per developer account, dev-mode apps; 429 QUOTA_EXCEEDED) is distinct from rate limits; Spotify publishes no hard per-endpoint numbers ('subject to change'), so capacity planning beyond dev mode is opaque.
Spotify has progressively restricted the dev-mode API surface (premium-only behavior, removed endpoints); verify the exact endpoints your agent needs still exist for dev-mode apps with a live test.
The Developer Policy states quotas are at Spotify's discretion, processing times are not guaranteed, and access can be revoked on review; extended quota covers only the reviewed use case.
Design Guidelines compliance (attribution, how you display Spotify content) is part of the ToS checkbox at creation and of any review.
prerequisites: A Spotify account (must hold Spotify Premium for development mode to function)
App name + description (shown to users on the consent screen)
Each tester's Spotify email for the 5-user allowlist

steps.detail: Log in at developer.spotify.com/dashboard > Create an App. Enter the app name and description, accept the Developer Terms of Service and Design Guidelines checkbox, CREATE. Instant; up to 25 apps per account.
steps.title: Create the app on the dashboard

steps.detail: The overview page shows the Client ID immediately; reveal the Client Secret and store it server-side. It goes in the Authorization: Basic base64(client_id:client_secret) header at the token endpoint.
steps.title: Save the client ID and secret

steps.detail: Edit Settings: add every Redirect URI your agent will use. This is an exact-match allowlist; the redirect_uri in the token exchange must exactly match the one in the authorize call. Optionally add Website and mobile bundle IDs.
steps.title: Register redirect URIs

steps.detail: Settings > Users Management > Add new user (name + Spotify email). Development mode allows up to 5 authenticated users total; anyone else gets a 403 on API calls.
steps.title: Allowlist your test users

steps.detail: GET accounts.spotify.com/authorize (response_type=code, client_id, redirect_uri, scope, state) > user consents > code returns to your redirect URI > backend POSTs accounts.spotify.com/api/token with grant_type=authorization_code. You get a 1-hour access token + refresh token. Request scopes per call from the published scope list (e.g. user-read-private, playlist-read-private, user-top-read).
steps.title: Implement the Authorization Code flow

steps.detail: Settings > Quota extension Request: partner application first, then the 4-step questionnaire. Spotify's review team evaluates compliance with the Developer Policy and replies by email. Scopes lock to what was requested at review time; adding scopes later needs a separate extension request.
steps.time: Questionnaire prep + up to 6 weeks waiting
steps.title: (If eligible) Request extended quota

tagline: Setup takes 15 minutes, but serving more than 5 users is structurally blocked: quota extension currently requires an established org with 250k+ monthly active users.

time.active: 15-30 min to a working dev-mode integration
time.total: Under an hour to dev mode; no realistic path to general availability for a new indie/agent builder today
time.waiting: Up to 6 weeks for a quota-extension review (stated by Spotify), IF you qualify
